headline: Recommended approving only the first year of the Pawtucket teachers' contract; School Committee to take another look at years two and three.
summary: The meeting covered a three-year contract with the Pawtucket Teachers' Alliance, which covers 715 teachers, and school finances. Officials discussed the fund balance, substitute and sick day costs, and Right-to-Read requirements. Councilor Wildenhain recommended approving only the first year of the contract.

THE COMMITTEE OF THE WHOLE AND THE FINANCE COMMITTEE TOOK UP THE 
FOLLOWING: 
 
Contract between the Pawtucket School Committee and the Pawtucket Teachers’ 
Alliance, Local 930, A.F.T., A.F.L.-C.I.O., for the period beginning September 1, 2026 through 
August 31, 2029 
 
Present for this portion of the meeting was Joanne Bonollo, Chair, Pawtucket School 
Committee; James T. Chellel Jr. , Pawtucket School Committee Member; Randy A. Buck, 
Superintendent, Pawtucket School Depa rtment; Stephanie DeMaio, Chief Financial Officer, 
Pawtucket School Department; and Carey Edwards, Controller, Pawtucket School Department. 
 
Ms. DeMaio provide d answers to the questions that the Finance Committee asked on 
September 23, 2026.

She stated that there are 1068 employees in the school department and 715 teachers covered by 
this contract. 
 
The fund balance as of th e end of FY 2024/25 was $17,822,591.  In the FY 2025/26 year, 
$4,626,991 was used to support the general fund leaving about $13,195,600 before the close -
out of the FY 2025/2026 year.  
 
She stated that there is no 5-year plan at this time.  They are waiting  to see where they are right 
now before starting a 5-year plan. 
 
Regarding how they will fund the additional $17 mi llion in the three -year contract, Ms. 
DeMaio stated that they will incorporate contract costs into mul ti-year planning, evaluate 
reserves, bu dget capacity, state and local revenues and other sources, while monitoring 
expenditures, enrollment and identifying efficiencies. 
 
When reviewing the multi -year financial plan regarding use of surplus and other practices, 
President Mercer asked what her comfort level of success was. 
 
Ms. DeMaio stated that difficult decisions will have to be made and they expect some 
challenges.  She believes they will be able to control some items that weren’t controlled before.  
They will look at areas they can pull back on, in order to make this happen. 
 
When providing clarification on Section 24, Certified/Licensed Personnel Safety and Protection 
from Harassment – the right to leave a meeting in which prohibited behavior occurs ; Ms. 
Bonollo stated that if a parent haras ses a teacher, they can stop the meeting and shut off the 
parent communication system.  It would then go to the administrator and then to the 
superintendent.  Mr. Chellel stated that this section required the administration to take on any 
harassing behavior on school grounds or on school issued technology.   
 
Regarding obligations beyond the three -year contract, issues such as enrollment, staffing, class 
size, special education, substitute coverage costs, right-to-read costs, healthcare and others need 
to be monitored. 
 
There is a policy that administrators should receive higher pay than the highest paid teachers. 
 
Ms. DeMaio stated in in 2025, the cost for substitutes was $1,843,081.  Coverage cost was 
$354,639.  Sick days cost $3,730,371.  In FY24, absence  figure for Pawtucketwas 24.3%.  Last 
year, statewide, it was about 8%. 
 
There are 64 teachers with outstanding Right -to-Read requirements, which could require up to 
eight days of training per teacher, depending on the needed requirements.  This could cost  up to 
$65,000 in class coverage costs and $22,500 in supplies.

President Mercer stated that the Right -to-Read requirem ents should have been up to date, 
because now it is causing teachers to be absent who must satisfy these requirements. 
 
Ms. DeMaio reviewed the medical reserve fund and stated that she would suggest using $1.8 
million of the reserve this year. 
 
Councilor Araujo asked how the School Department plans to make up the deficit, which would 
be approximately $7.2 million, in year two?  
 
Superintendent Buck stated that the School Department would ask the City for increased 
contributions. 
 
Mr. Chellel stated that the  teachers had extra minutes added to their work day , 10 minutes the 
first year and a total of 20 minutes over the three years.   The teachers received smaller class 
size, the contract has more structure on absenteeism, and language regarding the need to 
redistrict schools.   
 
Councilor Wildenhain expressed his concern about the affordability of this contract.  He would 
recommend approving the first year of the contract and have the School Committee take 
another look at years two and three.  The School Commit tee would have to bring this contract 
back to the teachers and then to the council for the one-year approval. 
 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:24 p.m.
